newsitem.title: USA: Premiere Tech unveils text-to-speech system. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Premiere Tech unveils text-to-speech system. [CORRECTED 19:25 GMT]

text.p: Premiere Technologies Inc said Tuesday it is unveiling a suite of services that allows a user to receive phone calls and messages, faxes, electronic mail and other communications from a single, integrated source.

The company said the system, known as Orchestrate, is a new class of network-based intelligent communications management that brings together phone and computer capabilties. Orchestrate will become available July 1.
The suite of services includes text-to-speech translation capabilities that allows a remote caller to automatically have electronic mail read over a phone.

The suite of services includes universal messaging with voice mail, faxes and electronic mail, follow-me single number services, conference calling, and content services such as news, weather and travel information.
An automated personal assistant organizes and routes the customer's messages.

"The marketplace is saturated with mind-boggling advances in technology -- new gadgets, new services, new hardware, new software and lots of new numbers, addresses, mailboxes and message centers," Premiere Chief Executive Boland Jones said in a statement.
"The beauty of Orchestrate is being able to listen to your e-mail over the phone or hear your voice mail through your computer," he said.
With Orchestrate, users can send electronic mail, voice, paging or fax messages over any telephone or personal computer with an Internet connection.
Users can hear their e-mail over the phone utilizing Premiere's proprietary text-to-speech software. The technology is based on a computer board from Dialogic Inc, a Premiere spokesman said.
Computer users also can retrieve voice mail messages from a computer screen.
The various Orchestrate services, along with the user's data, are managed and maintained on Premiere's own proprietary network-based platform, rather than on a local computer or telephone system.

Orchestrate customers can import information from electronic contact manager like Symantec Corp's ACT! software program and store it on the Premiere network, giving the user access to such information via the phone.
